added_lemmas.statement: Can one construct, for every \(N\) and every allowed actual design \(\mathcal S_N\), a terminating certified numerical approximation, with a proved error bound, to the continuum maximum defining \(c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\)?
added_lemmas.justification: The proved attainment and uniform continuity of \(c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\) do not by themselves provide an effective algorithm with a certified approximation error.
added_lemmas.gap: A computable two-sided description of the physical parameter set and a quantitative modulus for the Gaussian quantile optimization are unavailable under the frozen assumptions.
added_lemmas.consumer: A solution would turn the exact mathematical calibration into a terminating certified implementation on each allowed actual design.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct a terminating certified numerical approximation, with a proved error bound, to the continuum maximum defining c_{N,alpha}^{att} on every allowed actual design.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen assumptions give abstract compactness and uniform continuity but no effective two-sided representation of the determinant-constrained physical set, no certified feasible inner witnesses, and no computable convergence modulus for the Gaussian quantile optimization.
open_obligations.attempted: Outward interval enclosures can provide conservative upper values, but without certified inner feasibility and a quantitative modulus they do not certify the exact maximum or a prescribed approximation error; therefore no terminating rate such as N^{-1} is claimed.
open_obligations.partial_result: The exact maximum c_{N,alpha}^{att} is attained, its reference quantile map is uniformly continuous on the proved compactification, and 0<c_0<=c_{N,alpha}^{att}<=chi^2_{2,1-alpha} uniformly. For each fixed input pair (lambda,p), the defining three-dimensional Gaussian probability is explicit. These facts establish mathematical existence and a conservative analytic upper bound, but not a terminating certified approximation of the continuum maximum.

prose_updates.tldr: High-frequency separation can identify a spatial slope even without nugget variation, but existing theory does not justify confidence sets when the signed cross-tail shrinks to zero and its exponent disappears. Three exact affine-annihilating local slopes generate a finite-dimensional mean cone \(\beta\mathbf 1+B_Nq_N(p)\) whose secants and tangents remain uniformly separated from the slope direction. The central theorem derives the corresponding Gaussian experiment and feasible scale studentization on the actual quasi-uniform design. The exact attained least-favorable Gaussian critical value then yields asymptotic observed-law lower-envelope coverage equal to \(1-\alpha\) and pathwise \(O(N^{-1/2})\) diameter through zero, bounded, divergent, endpoint, elbow, and nonconvergent-design regimes; root-\(N\) risk and a complete-data Gaussian lower bound match the estimation and honest-diameter rates. A terminating certified numerical approximation to the continuum critical-value maximum remains open, and no finite-sample observed-law exactness is claimed.

project_justification.fill: The project derives the actual-design Gaussian experiment, residual-scale studentization, conservative chi-square coverage, exact attained least-favorable Gaussian calibration with asymptotic observed-law lower-envelope coverage equal to \(1-\alpha\), pathwise root-\(N\) diameter, root-\(N\) risk, and matching honest lower bounds. The remaining computational question is a terminating certified approximation, with a proved error bound, to the continuum critical-value maximum.

prose_updates.honest_scope: The actual-design Gaussian experiment, conservative chi-square confidence theorem, exact attained least-favorable Gaussian calibration, root-\(N\) risk and diameter bounds, and matching rate lower bounds are the principal proved claims. Exactness at finite \(N\) applies only to the Gaussian reference statistic; observed-law lower-envelope coverage is asymptotic. A terminating certified numerical approximation of \(c_{N,\alpha}^{\mathrm{att}}\) remains open. The scope excludes nuggets, unknown marginal smoothness, nonstationarity, independent Fourier-coordinate approximations, and covariance classes broader than the stated signed bivariate Matérn family. The PM2.5 and COVID-19 use is conditional on empirical Matérn and quasi-uniform-design diagnostics and does not itself establish a nonparametric causal estimand.
